## 0) Reflex Quick Info

- Reflex is a React state-management library inspired by ClojureScript re-frame (event-driven updates, subscriptions for derived data, effects/coeffects for side effects).
- Install:
  - Runtime: `npm i @flexsurfer/reflex`
  - Devtools (dev only): `npm i -D @flexsurfer/reflex-devtools`
- Docs:
  - Main docs: [reflex.js.org/docs](https://reflex.js.org/docs)
  - Best practices: [reflex.js.org/docs/best-practices.html](https://reflex.js.org/docs/best-practices.html)
  - Packages: [@flexsurfer/reflex](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flexsurfer/reflex), [@flexsurfer/reflex-devtools](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flexsurfer/reflex-devtools)

## 1) State Architecture

Use this baseline structure:

```text
src/state/
  runtime.ts
  event-ids.ts
  events.ts
  effect-ids.ts
  effects.ts
  sub-ids.ts
  subs.ts
```

Rules:
- Keep IDs centralized in `event-ids.ts`, `effect-ids.ts`, `sub-ids.ts`.
- Create an explicit runtime in `runtime.ts` with `createReflexRuntime({ initialState })`.
- Express feature registrations as `runtime.registerModule((scope) => { ... })`; keep and invoke its disposer for lazy loading/HMR.
- Mount React below `<ReflexProvider runtime={runtime}>`. The package-root API remains available only as the single-runtime compatibility facade.
- Instance `runtime.dispatch` and effect-context dispatch throw on unregistered event ids — register before dispatching. `dispatchSync` is restricted to the testing/admin harness. React `useSubscription` reads through the provider binding and throws on unregistered subscription ids.
- If `events.ts` or `subs.ts` grows too large, split by feature, keep shared/global state separate.

## 2) State Shape

- Grow horizontally (new top-level feature keys), avoid deep nesting.
- Keep UI state explicit and separate from domain entities. Use a plain prefix on field names to group by domain (e.g. `uiSidebarOpen`, `uiSelectedTab`, `uiModalVisible` for UI state; `todosMap`, `todosFilter` for domain state). Avoid separators like `/` or `.` in field names — flat `camelCase` with a domain prefix keeps keys simple, grep-friendly, and avoids issues with object path accessors.
- If using `Map`/`Set` in STATE, call `enableMapSet()` before creating the runtime.

## 3) Events `regEvent`

- Events must be synchronous and focused on state transitions.
- Events should read all required data from `draftState` (or via coeffects) — never rely on callers passing subscription-derived state; dispatch calls from views should only carry user intent (IDs, input values, flags).
- Validate inputs and guard clauses first; return early on invalid state.
- Mutate only required fields on `draftState`.
- Avoid unnecessary object/array recreation (`{...obj}`, `[...arr]`) when no actual change is needed.
- Never perform async/API/localStorage work directly in events.
- Return effect tuples for side effects.
- Draft values returned inside an effect payload are snapshotted automatically: `return [['storage/set', draftState.todos]]` is safe, and so is a draft on a field of a small wrapper object. The runtime deliberately does not unwrap a draft nested inside an array/Map/Set or several objects deep — development warns when one gets through, and those need an explicit `current(...)`.
- A dispatched event and its payload belong to the runtime from the `dispatch` call onward. The event runs on a later task, so mutating a value after dispatching it changes what the handler eventually sees. Dispatch values the caller will not touch again; development deep-freezes dispatched events so a violation throws at the mutation site instead of corrupting the event silently. This applies to `debounceAndDispatch`/`throttleAndDispatch` too.
- Prefer deterministic coeffects (time/id/random/env) instead of direct globals for testability.
- `dispatch` is async (queued; on the next animation-frame flush the subscription graph settles and listeners run synchronously inside that scheduled flush task). The testing/admin harness's `dispatchSync` commits and notifies subscribers before returning — use it only where that timing is load-bearing. Never call `dispatchSync` from inside an event handler (it throws) — return a `['dispatch', ...]` effect instead. Calling plain `dispatch` from inside a handler warns in dev for the same reason: emit follow-up events through the `['dispatch', ...]` effect.

Event naming:
- Keep exported constant keys in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Use namespaced string values: `feature/action` (example: `bases/create`).
- Keep key and value aligned:
  - `BASES_CREATE` -> `bases/create`
  - `PRODUCTION_PLAN_ADD_BUILDINGS_TO_BASE` -> `production_plan/add_buildings_to_base`

For compile-checked dispatch payloads, declare the typed payload maps (section 12) — with them, a wrong or missing payload is a `tsc` error instead of a runtime surprise.

## 4) Effects and Coeffects

- Put all I/O here: localStorage, HTTP, timers, analytics, navigation.
- Effects should be small, defensive, and fail-soft (log, do not crash app state flow).

## 5) Subscriptions `regRootSub` and `regSub`

- Define direct top-level state subscriptions first with `regRootSub(id, "pathKey")`.
- Define computed subscriptions with `regSub(id, depsFn, computeFn)` — arguments follow evaluation order.
- `computeFn` receives the dependency values as one array, in the order `depsFn` returns them, then the subscription's own params: `regSub(id, () => [['a'], ['b']], ([a, b], param) => ...)`. Adding a dependency therefore never shifts a param's position, and a reordered dependency list is a type error rather than a silent argument swap.
- Build derived subscriptions from other subscriptions only.
- Use parameterized subscriptions for by-id and section-specific queries.
- Subscription params must be plain JSON-serializable values (ids, strings, numbers). Never pass `Map`/`Set`/`RegExp`, functions, `undefined`, Symbols, BigInt, `NaN`/`Infinity`, or circular structures as params (at any nesting depth) — subscription caching and re-subscription key on `JSON.stringify(subVector)`, so such params collide, go stale, or throw (reflex warns in dev).
- Keep subscriptions deterministic and lightweight.
- Subscriptions must return data shaped and ready for direct view consumption — all filtering, sorting, formatting, and joining should happen in the subscription layer, not in React components.
- Move heavy computations to events (precompute once, read many); avoid repeated expensive derivations in hot subscriptions.
- Computed subs gate update propagation with deep equality by default — O(result size) per recompute. For subs returning large derived collections, pass a cheaper check: `regSub(id, depsFn, computeFn, { equalityCheck: shallowEqual })` (`shallowEqual` is exported from reflex). Immer's structural sharing keeps unchanged rows identical, so a shallow element-by-element check is usually enough.
- For typed `useSubscription` params and results, declare a runtime contract (section 12).

## 6) React Component Contract

- Components should only:
  - subscribe to minimal required data
  - dispatch events on user intent (pass only user-provided values — e.g. input text, selected id — never forward subscription data back through dispatch; the event handler should read everything it needs from the STATE itself)
  - render UI
- Always pass the component name as the second argument to `useSubscription` for devtools tracing:
  `const todos = useSubscription<Todo[]>([SUB_IDS.TODOS], 'TodoList');`
- Never transform, filter, sort, or reshape subscription data inside a component — if the view needs a different shape, create a dedicated subscription that returns it ready to render.
- Use direct React hooks only for local/ephemeral component concerns:
  - temporary form/input draft state before dispatch (alternative: bind the input value to a subscription and `dispatchSync` in `onChange` — the sync flush keeps the controlled input in step with the keystroke)
  - UI-only toggles scoped to one component (hover/open/focus)
  - refs, DOM measurement, animation lifecycle
- Do not mirror runtime-owned Reflex state in `useState`/`useReducer`.
- If state is shared, persisted, or business-relevant, keep it in Reflex STATE via events/subscriptions.
- Keep `useEffect` thin in components; business side effects belong in Reflex effects/coeffects.
- Do not place business rules/validation pipelines in component handlers.
- Avoid over-subscription (row/item components should not subscribe to full collections).

## 7) Devtools Setup

Install devtools as a dev dependency:

```bash
npm i -D @flexsurfer/reflex-devtools
```

Enable in your app entry point (`main.tsx`) before dispatching any events:

```ts
import { enableDevtools } from '@flexsurfer/reflex-devtools';
import { createReflexInspector } from '@flexsurfer/reflex/devtools';

enableDevtools(createReflexInspector(runtime));  // explicit development adapter

```

this code should be run only in dev env.

## 8) Test Minimum

For every new feature:
- Event tests: mutation correctness + emitted effect tuples.
- Subscription tests: derived outputs from fixed state fixtures.

Events and subscriptions are pure functions. In explicit-runtime code, install the feature on a fresh runtime per test. Handler lookup belongs to the test harness; the production runtime deliberately does not expose its live registry.

### Testing Events

Use the test harness's read-only handler lookup to get the raw handler after installing the feature. Build a mock `coeffects` object with `draftState` (and any injected coeffects), call the handler, then assert mutations on `draftState` and the returned effect tuples.

```ts
import type { EventHandler, CoEffects } from '@flexsurfer/reflex';
import { createReflexTestHarness } from '@flexsurfer/reflex/testing';
import './events'; // side-effect import registers handlers

const testHarness = createReflexTestHarness(runtime);

it('ADD_TODO should add a todo and persist', () => {
  const handler = testHarness.getEventHandler(EVENT_IDS.ADD_TODO) as EventHandler;

  const mockSTATE = { todos: [], showing: 'all' };
  const coeffects = {
    event: [EVENT_IDS.ADD_TODO, 'Buy milk'],
    draftState: mockSTATE,
    now: 12345,
  } as CoEffects;

  const effects = handler(coeffects, 'Buy milk');

  // Assert state mutation
  expect(mockSTATE.todos).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(mockSTATE.todos[0]).toEqual({ id: 12345, title: 'Buy milk', done: false });

  // Assert emitted effects
  expect(effects).toEqual([[EFFECT_IDS.SET_TODOS, mockSTATE.todos]]);
});

it('ADD_TODO should ignore empty input', () => {
  const handler = testHarness.getEventHandler(EVENT_IDS.ADD_TODO) as EventHandler;

  const mockSTATE = { todos: [], showing: 'all' };
  const coeffects = { event: [EVENT_IDS.ADD_TODO, '  '], draftState: mockSTATE, now: 1 } as CoEffects;

  const effects = handler(coeffects, '  ');

  expect(mockSTATE.todos).toHaveLength(0);
  expect(effects).toBeUndefined();
});
```

### Testing Subscriptions
Computed subscriptions: call `handler(inputFromParentSub1, inputFromParentSub2, ...)` directly — the handler receives its parent subscription values as positional arguments.

```ts
import type { SubHandler, SubDepsHandler } from '@flexsurfer/reflex';
import { createReflexTestHarness } from '@flexsurfer/reflex/testing';
import './subs';

const testHarness = createReflexTestHarness(runtime);

it('OPEN_COUNT computed sub counts active todos', () => {
  const handler = testHarness.getSubscriptionHandler(SUB_IDS.TODOS_OPEN_COUNT) as SubHandler;
  const todos = [
    { id: 1, title: 'A', done: false },
    { id: 2, title: 'B', done: true },
    { id: 3, title: 'C', done: false },
  ];

  expect(handler(todos)).toBe(2);
});
```

## 9) AI Generation Checklist

Before finalizing generated code:
- IDs added/updated in all relevant `*-ids.ts` files.
- Event namespaced and descriptive.
- Side effects isolated to effects/coeffects.
- `current(...)` used when passing draft-derived data to effects.
- No unnecessary object/array recreation in events.
- Expensive work not placed in frequently re-run subscriptions.
- Subscriptions return view-ready data; components do not reshape subscription output.
- Dispatch calls from components pass only user intent, not subscription data; events read from STATE.
- Tests added for new event/subscription behavior.

## 10) Working in an Existing Reflex Codebase (context-efficient navigation)

A Reflex app is fully indexed by its ID files. Follow this protocol instead of exploring or reading whole files — it keeps the required context small no matter how large the project is.

Build the map from IDs, not from code:
- Read the `*-ids.ts` files first. Together they are a complete index of everything the app can do (events), every side effect it performs (effects), and every view of its state (subs). Do not read `events.ts`/`subs.ts` end-to-end.
- Read `state.ts` for the state shape. IDs + state shape are usually all the context needed to plan a change.

Find code by exact-match grep, never by browsing:
- Implementation: grep `regEvent(EVENT_IDS.TODOS_ADD` or `regSub(SUB_IDS.TODOS_LIST` — exactly one match.
- Call sites: grep the constant (`EVENT_IDS.TODOS_ADD`) — its dispatch sites are the only UI triggers; `SUB_IDS.X` finds every consuming component via `useSubscription`.
- Every ID appears in exactly three roles: definition (ids file), one registration, and call sites. Apart from the application-level `ReflexProvider` runtime boundary, there is no per-feature provider or middleware wiring to trace.

Read only the handler, trust the contract:
- Event handlers are pure: inputs = coeffects + event params, outputs = `draftState` mutations + returned effect tuples. Nothing outside the function body changes its behavior, so reading the one function is sufficient to understand or safely modify it.
- Subscription `computeFn` receives exactly the parent sub values declared in `depsFn`, as one array in declaration order — the data-flow graph is declared, not inferred.
- Views only subscribe/dispatch/render. Changing state logic never requires reading component code, and changing markup never requires reading handlers.

Bounded file sets for common tasks:
- New behavior: add event ID → handler in `events.ts` → (optional) effect → dispatch from view.
- New derived data: add sub ID → `regSub` → `useSubscription` in component.
- State shape change: `state.ts` + root subs + handlers touching that key (grep the state key).
- State bug: reproduce → devtools event trace (event sequence + Immer patches show exactly which event wrote what) → read that one handler. Prefer the trace over reading code.
- Failed events are visible in traces with a normalized error shape (`phase`, `message`, `stack`, plus `interceptor`/`direction` or `effect`): an event whose handler/interceptor threw carries `tags.error` with `phase: 'handler'`; dispatching an unregistered event id produces a trace with `tags.error.phase: 'missing-handler'`; effects that threw after a committed event are listed in `tags.effectErrors` with `phase: 'effect'`. Check these tags before assuming a dispatch worked.
- If the `reflex-devtools` MCP server is connected, call `app_status` first, select the intended `runtimeId`, and use the per-runtime tools instead of reading code: `get_state` (current state, supports path), `get_active_subs` (computed sub values), `get_handlers` (all registered event/fx/cofx/sub ids — a runtime index of the app), and `get_traces` (events, sub runs, renders, timings). Pass `runtimeId` to every call when multiple runtimes are connected. `dispatch_event` is always listed but succeeds only after an explicit `--allow-dispatch` grant; DevTools is read-only by default.

Keep the index self-documenting:
- Put a one-line signature comment on each ID so the ids file alone is enough to dispatch or subscribe correctly, without opening handlers:

```ts
export const EVENT_IDS = {
  /** (title: string) — add todo, persists via storage/set_todos */
  TODOS_ADD: 'todos/add',
} as const;

export const SUB_IDS = {
  /** (id: string) => Todo | undefined */
  TODO_BY_ID: 'todos/by_id',
} as const;
```

- When adding or changing a handler's params, update its signature comment — the ids files are the API docs that later sessions (and other agents) rely on.

## 11) Explicit runtime starter

Reflex never creates a package-global runtime. Construct the application
runtime once, register every feature on it, and provide that same instance to
React.

```ts
import {
  createReflexRuntime,
  current,
  ReflexProvider,
  useSubscription,
} from '@flexsurfer/reflex';

type Todo = { id: string; text: string; done: boolean };

export const runtime = createReflexRuntime({
  initialState: { todos: [] as Todo[] },
  runtimeId: 'todos',
});

runtime.registerModule((registrar) => {
  registrar.regEffect('storage/set_todos', (todos: Todo[]) => {
    localStorage.setItem('todos', JSON.stringify(todos));
  });

  registrar.regEvent('todos/add', ({ draftState }, text: string) => {
    const clean = text.trim();
    if (!clean) return;
    draftState.todos.push({ id: `todo_${Date.now()}`, text: clean, done: false });
    return [['storage/set_todos', current(draftState.todos)]];
  });

  registrar.regRootSub('todos/list', 'todos');
  registrar.regSub(
    'todos/open_count',
    () => [['todos/list']],
    ([todos]: [Todo[]]) => todos.filter((todo) => !todo.done).length,
  );
});

// app.tsx
export function AppRoot() {
  return <ReflexProvider runtime={runtime}><App /></ReflexProvider>;
}

// TodoList.tsx
const todos = useSubscription<Todo[]>(['todos/list']);
runtime.dispatch(['todos/add', 'Buy milk']);
```
## 12) Typed Contracts (opt-in compile-time checking)

A contract is one `ReflexContracts` declaration describing the runtime's state, event payloads, effect payloads, and subscriptions. Declaring it turns `tsc` into a wiring verifier — typo'd ids, wrong payloads, wrong subscription usage, invalid effect tuples, and unknown state keys become compile errors. While undeclared, the whole API stays permissive and everything above works as written.

Declare it next to the ids files (e.g. `src/contracts.ts`) and pass it to the runtime:

```ts
import type { ReflexContracts } from '@flexsurfer/reflex/vanilla';
import type { Showing, Todo, TodoState } from './state';
import { EVENT_IDS } from './event-ids';
import { SUB_IDS } from './sub-ids';

export interface AppContracts extends ReflexContracts {
  state: TodoState;
  events: {
    [EVENT_IDS.TODOS_ADD]: [title: string];
    [EVENT_IDS.TODOS_TOGGLE]: [id: string];
  };
  effects: {
    'storage/set_todos': Todo[];
    'ui/scroll_top': void; // no payload -> the tuple is just ['ui/scroll_top']
  };
  subscriptions: {
    [SUB_IDS.TODOS_LIST]: { params: []; result: Todo[] };
    [SUB_IDS.TODO_BY_ID]: { params: [id: string]; result: Todo | undefined };
  };
}

export const runtime = createReflexRuntime<AppContracts>({ initialState: createState() });
export const { useSubscription } = createReflexHooks<AppContracts>();
```

Using the id constants as computed keys keeps one source of truth: an id cannot drift between its declaration, its registration, and its call sites.

Every section is optional — adopt them one at a time; a missing or empty section stays permissive.

What this changes:
- `dispatch([EVENT_IDS.TODOS_ADD, title])` — id must be declared, payload must match the tuple. Also applies to `debounceAndDispatch`/`throttleAndDispatch`.
- `regEvent(EVENT_IDS.TODOS_ADD, ({ draftState }, title) => ...)` — handler params and `draftState` are inferred, with no generics. Undeclared ids stay permissive in `regEvent`.
- Effect tuples returned from handlers are checked: declared ids with matching payloads only. The built-in `'dispatch'` and `'dispatch-later'` effects are always available, their ids are reserved, and their event vectors are checked against the event map — so `return [['dispatch', [EVENT_IDS.X, payload]]]` gets the same checking as a direct `dispatch`. `regEffect` infers the handler's value param.
- `regSub(id, depsFn, computeFn)` — dependency values are inferred from `depsFn` and the result is checked against the declared result type.
- `useSubscription([SUB_IDS.TODO_BY_ID, id])` — params checked and result inferred, no explicit generic.
- `createReflexTestHarness(runtime)` exposes state reads, flush, and non-React subscription inspection for tests.

Single-runtime apps: the package-level `useSubscription` cannot take a type argument, because a React context type is fixed at creation. Bind it once by augmenting the ambient anchor, which is the same `ReflexContracts` shape:

```ts
declare module '@flexsurfer/reflex' {
  interface DefaultContracts extends AppContracts {}
}
```

Apps owning several runtimes should skip the anchor and use `createReflexHooks<AppContracts>()` per runtime, since one ambient default cannot describe two runtimes.

Rules:
- Event and subscription params must be tuples; use `[]` for no params. Use labeled tuple members (`[title: string]`) — they double as documentation. Effect payloads are single values; use `void` for effects with no payload.
- Once a section is declared it is closed: every id used against that surface must appear in it. Keep the maps complete — they double as the app's API manifest.
- Keep the maps in sync with the ids files: one entry per id, same naming.
